page: Amazon Web Services r6i.32xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C) clocked at 3.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 1024 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, offering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Networking capabilities include a 50 Gbps baseline throughput. There is no bundled local instance storage and no integrated GPU accelerators.

In compute benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong multi-threaded capabilities, scoring in the top decile for PassMark overall CPU, extended vector instructions, and encryption tasks. Multi-core Geekbench and stress-ng tests place the server within the top 25% of measured systems, complemented by high uncached memory read bandwidth exceeding 334 GB/s. In operational testing, the instance records over 107 million Redis SET operations per second and strong throughput in clang software compilation and static web delivery. Single-thread execution across Geekbench and compression tasks aligns with median benchmark tiers.

Because the instance provides no ephemeral local NVMe storage, all persistent disk IOPS and storage bandwidth rely entirely on network-attached Amazon EBS volumes. Additionally, text generation throughput on larger LLM models drops into lower percentiles due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. The r6i.32xlarge offers high resource density for consolidating large-scale enterprise environments. Appropriate workloads include distributed in-memory caching platforms such as Redis or Memcached, large-scale relational databases, real-time analytics engines, and heavy multi-threaded enterprise application tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services r6i.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the platform delivers 1024 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no onboard local storage, depending entirely on remote block storage, and contains no discrete GPUs. In benchmarking evaluations, the configuration achieves top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust memory read bandwidth, and elevated throughput in cryptographic extensions and Redis database operations, while single-core performance registers within median tiers. Text generation on large language models is constrained without hardware acceleration. The r6i.32xlarge is structurally tailored for enterprise workloads demanding extensive memory capacity, such as large in-memory databases, real-time analytics clusters, caching nodes, and high-concurrency corporate applications.
